so grateful that my dentist recommended carly and orofacial myology! this is not regular speech therapy.... though, it probably should be something all speech therapists are certified in. actually, dare i share, that it should be something all pediatricians, school admins, teachers, speech therapists, dentists, and orthodontists are taught about and should intern in at the very least.
both of my kids looked completely normal from the outside, but had challenges with how their mouth was forming and (as it turns out) facial/jaw/tongue/etc. neuro-muscular control challenges. the visual observation of teeth was only the tip of the iceberg. without going into lots of details, there were speaking, eating, breathing, tongue and lip ties, drooling, tongue thrust, tooth crowding, cross bite, over bite, under bite, and swallowing challenges. we were looking at orthodontists and surgical options by the time my oldest was 6 years old. all i could foresee was debt, time, lots of therapy, and metal mouths for the next 20 years. looking back now, as i write this, i wonder how i thought some braces and time would fix all this.
carly spoke about orofacial myology at a dental conference my pediatric dentist attended. our pediatric dentist had been our dentist for a couple years and had even consulted orthodontists about my kids. after learning from carly, she recommended this therapy for both kids before i got ortho/surgical quotes.
i am so glad she did. carly did an assessment and found some serious challenges. skeptical as i was, she reviewed results of this type of therapy with me and explained that both kids were having neuro-muscular challenges that could be managed to change the shape of their mouth and teeth, breathing, etc. i saw pictures of results and carly made me feel comfortable with her recommendations. after our consult, i came to the conclusion that with this therapy, my kids might not have to have braces or surgery, and that this would help indefinitely for the rest of their lives, so we started therapy that week.
after only 2 weeks of therapy, all signs of sleep apnea were gone and my son hadn't choked on his food at all. (i hadn't put 2:2 together- that breathing challenges and other issues while sleeping were signs of sleep apnea, until it stopped. neither had the pediatrician.) 
carly is so good with kids and personable, using food, straws, mirrors, even toys to get the kids thru the therapy sessions and want to continue practicing at home.
after 4 months carly showed me a side-by-side picture of the mouths of both kids before therapy and after the 4 months. if it wasn't zoomed in from their full face, i don't think i would have said they were from the same people. after 1 year, our pediatric dentist retook xrays and pulled me aside. she told me she needed to talk to carly asap because she'd never seen such natural, results. she said she never would have said (in comparing last year's xrays to this year's), that they were from the same people.
since the 2nd xrays were taken, my older child has lost all but 4 baby teeth. there's now plenty of room for her adult teeth, and they are coming in and straightening out on their own. for both kids, the apnea, ties, crowding, choking, and cross/under bites are gone. we are still working on the speech part, but that'll come in time, the little one's still pretty young.
thank you carly. i appreciate you and wish orofacial myology was something more people in the us understood, recommended, and used in regular practice.

i am writing this review right after leaving, so it is fresh in my mind. 
i have a 15 year old with a bizarre needle phobia.... like off the charts. she had a bleeding disorder as a young child that involved weekly blood draws. the draws just never went well, and as each one happened, my kiddo became more and more damaged. 
don't get me wrong, my daughter is tough. like she will shoulder thump a bigger kid for being a bully. she is not scared of a single thing in the world. she has taken on steep skiing slopes, and handled herself in a raft going down a class five. 
but pop her in a doctor office with a teeny tiny needle, and the girl is a freak-out, sobbing, kicking and screaming mess. it is bad.
over the years, we have gone to places for shots that have held her down, snuck up on her and criticized her to get the shots in her (zoomcare). so of course, all of these tactics have only made things worse. 
today i took her in for 3 vaccines. we have been a bit past due because of the issues. you see, metro peds won't give the shot without consent.
and so for the last 2 years, i have brought my kiddo in numerous times hoping that today would be the day. only with no luck, at all.
today we went in again. she was prepared. she had her numbing cream, she had done her self talk. she felt ready.
and once again, we spent an hour in the office, with no luck. i was so pissed! it was not one of my finer mommy moments.
you see, they told us that today was the last try, if she couldn't do it today then she would have to start exposure therapy with a behavioral health clinic. and as a single mom with three kids, one of which is currently dealing with some severe medical issues that require numerous weekly office visits - my brain just could not wrap around the idea of one more kid in my house requiring weekly doctor visits. 
i lost it. like legit. 
we left the office, and as we went into the hallway towards the elevator, my daughter was profusely apologizing. and, well, i just didn't care. i told her i knew i wasn't handling the moment well.... but come on! then she felt horrible and wanted to go back in, and i said no dice. "they told you that was it! they said no more office visits until you go through therapy!" and she was sobbing begging to go back and make it right. and i was crying.
this lovely lady came out of a side office door, and asked us to come into her office. i was immediately mortified. i glanced in her office door and saw the couch, the teddy bears, the boxes of tissues, along with the inspirational quotes on the wall - and i thought to myself "great, the shrink needs to see me now. awesome" i was absolutely mortified. 
i tried to pass, tell her we were fine, we would just be going home. but she insisted, and explained she was the clinic manger. she wanted to talk and find out how she could help. 
my daughter gladly stormed into her office, so i had no choice. and i was quickly feeling like the worst mom ever. 
the woman (i wish i caught her name), talked us through what was going on, and asked me if i would allow her to give olivia another chance at getting her shots. i figured, what a waste of time, but whatever. she seemed confident, i knew there was no way, but why not really prove to her how crazy the situation is. 
i just could not stop crying; between frustration, exhaustion, embarrassment... i was a mess.
she brought back the same ma that had already spent an hour trying to give my daughter her vaccines. they talked strategy, they came up with a plan. 
so... long story short. it took another hour, but my kiddo got her vaccines! and she walked out proud with her head high. and i walked out still crying but for so many other reasons. 
i am so grateful to this clinic. i have no idea where these ladies get their patience from, but they are saints. 
i really respect their "consent only" policy with shots. and i am so grateful that they did not give up on my girl. 
this is the best in the business, and a very safe place to take your children.

after our 95-year-old friend broke her hip and became bedbound, roze room hospice stepped in and took over her care. up to now, the healthcare from her insurer was mediocre at best and we all know how that goes. a parade of beleaguered lvns, nurses and doctors calling it in day in and day out, dealing with yet another patient and never really seeing the person beyond the body in front of them. 

roze room hospice was a breath of fresh air and our saviour. i don't know how we would have taken care of her without the tireless and loving care from them. from the get-go they knew exactly what to do, ordering a hospital bed and all the necessary accouterments for her comfort. they knew the drill--diapers and wipes, her meds, an over the bed table, bedrails, a nebulizer, even an air mattress to keep the bed sores away. within hours of roze room taking over, everything was delivered and put in place, setting the stage for her optimal care and comfort. 

the roze room staff was top notch. laura, joy, keith, dr. patel, eryn, gareth, irma, and libby were all ever so professional and had plenty of heart. like me, they became enamored by our friend and took the time to get to know her.  it showed in how she was treated-- with genuine kindness and heartfelt compassion from day one up until the day of her passing. after her passing, laura and some of the caregivers were kind enough to follow up with condolence texts and touching notes as if she were family.  laura even helped me with returning all of the medical equipment and instructed me on how to safely dispose of the unused medications. 

the one piece of  feedback i would give to roze room is that i wish we had better direct access to her care team via mobile phone and text. i can understand why patients have to go through the main number to get a hold of her caregivers, but direct access to them would have been so much better. that being said, the switchboard was extremely responsive and quick in getting our messages out to the caregivers and laura the rn was kind enough to give me her number so that i could call and text when i needed to. 

thank you roze room. so grateful that you were there for us!

okay, so i never post reviews for anything, but sohomd honestly changed my life not gonna lie. i originally signed up a year or two ago bc they took my insurance (cigna at the time, now aetna), and legally the only way i can get refills on the adhd medication i've been taking for most of my life is to meet with a doctor once a month. i was tired of having to trek to an office in the middle of the workday every month just to confirm my meds were still working, so i signed up for a video appointment with a random doctor here that specialized in adhd. little did i know that would end up totally changing my life.

the guy i got paired up with, dr robert weston, is by far the nicest, kindest, and most caring psychiatrist i have ever worked with. he listens to my needs, cares about my life, and has moved his schedule around to help me in emergencies. after a year of prescription management meetings, he helped me realize i had also been suffering from severe anxiety and depression, and that medication could perhaps help. i was so nervous, but took his suggestion, and it honestly is like i am living in a whole new world. i never knew that life could be so much less exhausting or that i could experience happiness like i do now. i had been living in a fugue state of crippling anxiety and doubt before, but i never would have known it without his help. 

he was so cautious in recommending a medication for me, and made sure to check in regularly after i started taking it to ensure it was going well. 

the one major problem with sohomd is that their administrative system is a hot mess, and there was a 4 month period of time where they suddenly couldn't accept aetna and blue cross due to a weird issue from the insurance companies' end (thankfully fixed as of jan 2020), but robert moved his schedule around to accommodate me anyway so he could make sure i was doing alright, and would call me directly to check in whenever something was going wrong from an admin perspective. 

the level of care i have received from him honestly makes all of the insurance and administrative shenanigans worth it. would highly recommend if you're looking for a caring, flexible psychiatrist, who you can video chat with from a conference room at the office in between work. idk about the other people who work here, but he rocks

short version: phenomenal clinic. i gave birth 8 weeks ago, right when covid-19 was squeezing ny by the throat. it was a natural birth, my baby is healthy, and my body is basically back to normal - all things made possible by the expert care and support of dr brennan and his partner jais. the cliff notes on this clinic are that it is exceptional - immaculate, outstanding patient care, quirky and kind bedside manners all round, and connected to the best hospital in nyc. i cannot recommend the practice highly enough. long version: i was recommended to dr brennan by my boss (an experienced attorney who doesn't suffer fools), after i lamented the prevalence of arrogant, impersonal doctors. "you will love the brennans," my boss said. "they are eccentric, experienced, won't push an agenda, they'll give you all the time in the world, and will make you feel like family." she was right on all counts. the brennans invest seriously in their patients. throughout my pregnancy, they discussed each decision point in depth, teasing out the best path forward. perhaps because i'm a lawyer, i saw the fact that they would discuss pros and cons in front of me as a sign of true professionalism - they weren't arrogant enough to think there was one right path, and they weren't afraid to test one another's views to make sure we got it right. no question was stupid, and even if my appointment was initially 15 minutes long, they would keep answering my questions for an hour if needed. dr brennan is permanently on call for his patients, and i contacted him regularly with concerns that usually amounted to nothing but which he treated with the utmost seriousness. yes, the flipside of this kind of personal care is that appointments sometimes start late, but i would rather wait for an appointment and have this level of attention than efficiently get bad service. (and to be fair, people like me regularly rock up 45 minutes late and throw their whole schedule out of whack...).

another important plus is that dr brennan is the only doctor. in so many practices you never see the same doctor more than twice, so when you are sick they don't have a point of comparison. (nothing like being told you're fine when you feel like death). this meant that when i showed up at dr brennan's office late at night in serious pain from my contractions, he could trust right away that i wasn't playing around and needed pain relief stat. he could also read me like a book during labour - eg he suggested i use a mirror because i'm goal-orientated (and yes, it was a huge motivator!), and he knew when he could push me to the next level during delivery and when i truly needed a break from the pain. i'll always be grateful to dr brennan for staying so in tune with me. i trusted him, and if he'd said i needed a c-section i would have gone with that whether i'd wanted to or not - childbirth is full of risks and curveballs, and that's why we have experts like him to give us their best bet.

dr brennan's connection to lenox hill hospital is also a major drawcard. the staff are extremely supportive and professional, and that was so important since i was only allowed one support person (because of corona). a few days after my birth i had to go to the er at a brooklyn hospital on a non-birth related matter, and the staff were horrific - cold, unprofessional, no ppe, and the only way i got through that was because dr brennan coordinated with the er doctors (and calmed me down!). 

post-partem, the brennans have also been incredible. they have seen me by zoom, and started me on treatment on magnetic chair that gives a bajillian pelvic floor exercises in a short amount of time - well worth it!

i was horrified to read a review that dr brennan is a 'yeller' and jais tries to cover up - what bizarre accusations. nothing could be further from the truth. dr brennan is calm, kind, and nothing is too difficult. jais is also a delight - hilarious and incredibly supportive. they are cautious but not overzealous with testing, and they never pressured me - eg i decided not to get the amnio or the late term scans, and there was never any pressure to do the contrary. i was bemused by the reviewer who questioned the regular internal and external ultrasounds - how do you think dr brennan is supposed to see what's going on? holistic fortune-telling? x-ray vision? psychic ability? (side note: i loved these ultrasounds - hearing my baby's heart beat each week was the most incredible part of pregnancy. why would anyone not want that??) 

thank you, dr brennan and jais, for being with me on this remarkable journey. if i have another baby i want you by my side again every step of the way!

leaving the house with a toddler during a pandemic is frightening, but having to go to an urgent care that is also a covid testing site is the last place a parent wants to be. 

my child fell and needed stitches. i called ahead and was told to come in. although the place was empty i waited to be seen by the physician almost a half hour because he was on a telemedicine call. 

the nursing assistant that came to take vitals did not wash her hands and only did so after i asked. i asked her to clean the oxiometer and she refused saying it was done and they didn't have a lot of patients that day, however i told her that i didn't feel comfortable unless i cleaned it so i pulled a lysol wipe out of my bag and cleaned it myself. 

dr. chao came in (also did not wash his hands as he was wearing gloves, and did put on a fresh pair when i asked) and looked at my child's wound and said my child may need stitches, he said that it was my call to make, however, he did recommend it.

i went with his advice and decided to proceed. he brought in an assistant and i asked if it possible to do this alone as i wanted to minimize risk. he said no. 

i saw that the physician and assistant were only equipped with a surgical mask, and would need to be within inches of my child, so i asked if it was possible that he wore a respirator or n95, to which he replied "i don't have one would you like to donate some to us" in a condescending tone.

i cannot believe that this is the level of ppe this facility has. i understand there is a shortage of ppe however, this should be standard for a facility that is a pediatric covid testing site. how is a covid testing site not equipped with n95's?! especially when the parent requests it. 

furthermore, he did not inform me until during the procedure that stitches raises the chance of infection. i was upset and told him that he should have disclosed this prior so that i could have made a more inform decision. he told me that there must have been miscommunication because he did (i assure you he did not). 

i really wonder if i made the right choice. it's not easy to decide if going to an urgent care is the right thing to do, and i really hoped that i would have had a better experience. 

i do believe it's important to be forthcoming with patients and let them know prior to coming that there is no proper ppe, especially when a medical supply company down the street sells n95's. (pico medical).

i called the office to report this incident and the office manager was friendly however i gave this some thought and wanted to be fully transparent so that other parents can make an informed decision on coming here. i wish i would have known i wouldn't have come here during a pandemic. now i'm left wondering did i do the right thing? would the ceo bring his child there with no ppe? it's a sad thing that this corporation hasn't outfitted its staff with the proper protection. 

fair warning for a parent. this is definitely something to consider. 

the one star was for the receptionist who was kind and made the check in process at the front desk go smoothly.

did you know that heart disease is the leading cause of death for men, women, and people of most racial and ethnic groups in the united states? another staggering fact is one person dies every 37 seconds in the united states from cardiovascular disease.  but, even more, frightening to me is knowing that heart disease is the leading cause of death in women.   just knowing these facts, i'm glad that dr. yamada is on my healthcare team at queens medical center.   i regard him as progressive, knowledgeable, compassionate yet straightforward with his explanations to me and i have been under his care for at least the past decade or longer.  

my scheduled annual office visits may include in-office treadmill stress tests or ekg in addition to getting my basic vital signs.  dr. yamada has also prescribed other diagnostic tests to help him to decide if he needs to recommend changes in my lifestyle or medication.  this time around, during pandemic restrictions, i participated in a telehealth visit.  this was my first-time using hmsa's online care application.  after registering for the application (on friday, in preparation for my monday appointment), i found this application easy-to-use and quite intuitive.   on monday morning, about 20 minutes prior to my designated appointment time, i signed in to the app's "waiting room".  then, about 3 minutes prior to my appointment time, dr. yamada's nurse signed me in to my appointment and dr. yamada made his appearance on-time as he usually does for office visits.

the telehealth visit was just as good as an in-person visit except that i had taken my own blood pressure and weight at home.  yeah, yeah... unfortunately, i had to report the "corona pounds" gains.  dr. yamada had reviewed the results of the blood draws that i had taken a couple of days prior to this appointment.  i guess that because of the pandemic concerns, he and his nurse were wearing face masks even for this session.  i liked that their office takes this pandemic seriously and takes all possible precautions to not only protect themselves but to protect their patients.    i sort of like this telehealth application as it was easy to use and i didn't even have to leave the comfort of my home.

anyway, i've already scheduled my next office visit in 2021 and look forward to the continued maintenance of good heart health through dr. yamada's recommendations.

during covid-19, right after the travel ban, i was on quarantine for 14 days since i arrived from europe on vacation.  during that time, i fell ill and after a few days under virtual care, my doctor advised me to go to the er.  i chose memorial hermann sugar land thinking i would get good care.  i was totally wrong.

once in the er, which was set up efficiently because of the virus, the er doctor immediately explained to me that they will not send my covid-19 test off to be tested unless i was admitted to the hospital.  his main concern was not diagnosing my problem but explaining that i would have to go somewhere else to get tested for covid-19.

i was advised to go the the er by my doctor because i was coughing excessively, barely able to breath, experiencing pain in my back when breathing and coughing, wheezing and extreme shortness of breath even with using an inhaler.  my temp stayed below 100.4 so it wasn't considered a fever.

the er began to run tests:  chest x-rays, ct scan, urine-analysis, blood-work, i.v., etc.

i waited about 45 minutes for all the test results to return and during that time, i suffered and tried to breath over and over in spite of the difficulties i was experiencing.  finally, the er doctor returned (dr. b. parker) and said that my lungs were clear and that the covid-19 swab would not be sent to the lab because i'm not being admitted to the hospital.  i stated that i understood about the swab but i didn't understand what was going on with my breathing so i asked him again about my lungs.  dr. parker repeated that my lungs were "all clear" and that there was no sign of the virus in my lungs. 

i asked the doctor what was he diagnosing me as having. since we know there's no sign of covid-19 in my lungs, what is it then and what was he going to give me to help me breath.   dr. parker turned the paper around and it read, "cough - adult".  i asked, "so you're diagnosing me as having a cough?"  he replied yes.  i was dumbfounded.  i came to the er with a cough and shortness of breath and now the dr. was telling me that i had a cough.  wow!  

i asked him what was he going to do about helping me?  he stated that he was calling in prescriptions to my pharmacy to take but to act like i had covid-10 and still isolate.  he stated that he believed it was just an allergy infection and that these meds would clear it up.  i informed him that i don't typically suffer with allergies and that i had been taking zyrtec because the virtual doctor i spoke to recommended it but i wasn't getting any better.  he reemphasized again that the test would not be sent and that if i wanted a covid-19 test, i needed to go to another site.  i asked about an antibiotic to clear up the infection and he said the meds he prescribed would clear up the infection.  i later learned that the meds were regular over-the-counter stuff that i had already been using that wasn't effective:  tylenol, mucinex and claritin-d.

i believe dr. parker's only concern was covid-19 and not finding the real source of my problems.  i asked my discharge nurse again about my lungs being "all clear" and she said well they are not all clear and that they had a haze over them.  i asked what does a haze mean.  she informed me that the doctor believes the haze is possibly from a bacteria infection from allergies so he's prescribed some meds to help.  i again said i don't suffer with allergies but ok the pollen is high so i guess.  

i was discharged and walked to my car still struggling to breath just the same way as i walked into the hospital.   

that was saturday, march 21st. fast forward to wednesday, march 25th and i was not feeling any better, in fact, i felt worse. i called my doctor both the 25th and 26th and left messages. her nurse called my back on the 27th and informed me to stop taking all allergy meds immediately and that she had reviewed the labs and x-rays and they believe that haze over my right lung is pneumonia.

pneumonia?!!  so i had pneumonia in the right lung for an additional 6 days without any treatment?!  why would dr. parker say i was "all clear" and ignore the haze?  i had to take additional time from work to heal whereas if dr. parker would have just taken the time to explore my results for something more than covid-19, he could have treated me correctly and i could have returned back to work without taking additional time.  

lastly, once i got the bill, i saw that i was billed $273.50 for a pregnancy test!!!  the admitting nurse asked if there was anyway i could be pregnant, i immediately answered no and explained why i couldn't be.  so why would you give me, a 49 yr old woman with a valid reason a pregnancy test?  especially for $273.50.  over billing???   yes!

i will never go back to memorial hermann sugar land emergency room.  the care of the treating physician was below sub-par and i could have saved way more time and money going to another facility.

i've had aud (alcohol use disorder) for about 40 years. i've tried everything: hypnosis, acupuncture, years on antabuse, 6 months and then 7 years sober in aa in 2000s. each relapse turned into a several weeks long binge, forcing me to seek help again. finally, in 2014 i discovered sinclair method (https://www.the-sinclair-method.com/), which turned out to be a lifesaver. my drinking quickly went down to safe limits and i started to have alcohol free days several times a week. for 5.5 years i was a social drinker, a "normie" in aa speak - until covid struck. 

i live alone, the lockdown made me seriously depressed. all my routines and nearly all social contacts were broken and it felt like a solitary confinement. at some point in april, i stopped taking my medication as prescribed by the sinclair method. from there, my drinking quickly escalated and turned into a heavy 6 weeks binge. by may 13 i had to go to er and then to a 10 days detox in holister; spent the first night in icu nearly having a heart attack. after i got back home on sunday may 24, i wanted to make sure that sinclaire is still working (i still had some meds left from my last refill); i had 3 drinks on the first day, then it went 1, 1, 0, 1, 0 - amazing, considering my condition before the detox. 

in the meantime, my gf discovered the intensive outpatient program (iop) at good sam behavioral. i was surprised to learn that dr cecil a. bradley, who prescribed me naltrexone all these years, is the medical director of this program. the program seemed very useful since a) it is in person, no zoom, b) i got a double diagnosis and could address my underlying emotional issues and c) i could get an extended medical leave, since i was not feeling up to getting back to work immediately. on thursday, may 28 i was there and talked to marcella (admissions) dr khan (sp? md), nurse diane and some other people. i was very open about what i've been doing before, what brought me there and about my intentions (go back on sinclaire, since it works great and aa stopped working for me at some point). everybody seemed to be open-minded, accepting and approving of my course of treatment. some even wrote down the name of my method and said they were curious and want to learn more about it.

thursday and friday sessions were pretty nice, with meditation, some cbt and open discussions on topics suggested by patients themselves. and then, on friday noon dr bradley showed up, took me to his office and told me that their program is based on full abstinence and if i keep up the  controlled drinking, i have to leave. he said there are alternatives to aa and suggested some other program - he just could remember it's name. he is in his 80s and seems to forget things. i promised to think about it over the weekend and tell him about my decision on monday. after all, at this point i could easily refrain from drinking for the duration of the program.

however, on monday my case manager handed me a recovery plan with mandatory conditions: attend at least 3 meetings a week, find a sponsor and report progress at each morning session. i told her i don't do aa, and i was told to go talk to dr bradley, and again he gave me a dilemma: full abstinence and meetings or leave the program. "there is this other program - can't remember it's name... rational recovery?" "- smart recovery?" "- yes, this must be it". "- i researched it, and it has about the same success rate as aa - which is in single digits - whereas sinclair method has success rate near 80%". "- i don't care. this program requires full abstinence and meetings". so i informed him that i'm quitting and went home.

there are several things that really upset and anger me. 
1) why did dr bradley prescribe my medicine all these years and even wrote me another 3 refills on that monday if he disapproves on sinclair method so much? 
2) how does a doctor refer a patient to some program the name of which he can't even remember? does he know anything about it? or he just doesn't care?
3) why did they admit me at all, knowing full well my intentions, knowing dr bradley's views and giving me false hopes? 
4) what kind of doctors put a patient into completely unscientific, faith-based programs with abysmal success rate and force him to abandon something that is proven to work for 80% and this patient in particular?

so i googled dr bradley and discovered that the medical board of california twice has suspended his license, once in 1990 and second time in 2007 (5 years probation). he also was known to be sending referrals to and working at a couple of shady rehabs ran by an uncertified drug addict.

makes you wonder, how does a doctor like cecil bradley ends up a medical director at well-respected hospital like good sam? i would not recommend going to good sam in- or outpatient behavioral programs until they replace him. the rest of staff seems to be ok, but there is nothing they could do to help me under current leadership.

long and lengthy but honest review:


results at week 1: 
today marks one week that i got prk eye corrective surgery and i am in the office for my first vision check with dr. law. she is amazing, kind and extremely knowledgeable. i asked her several questions and she was able to give me exact and detailed responses without me feeling rushed in any way. she preformed my eye exams twice. before removing my contacts and again after they were removed. my appointment lasted about 20 minutes and was over before it was even scheduled to start!(since i was early) i learned that my vision is at a (blurry) 20/25 and i was also cleared to drive. that's amazing improvement and i'm very pleased with my results thus far! 

for those worried about getting surgery during a pandemic: (because i was too) 
the office does a great job with cleanliness. there are very few patients in the waiting room at the same time, everyone sits at least one seat apart and they take your temperature as soon as you walk in! they are only allowing patients in the office and any family is asked to wait outside. they offer seating and the downstairs lobby also has a seating area if you wish to wait. (i live very close and always just got dropped off and picked up.) they also have lysol and hand sanitizer everywhere and definitely keep all areas very clean. everyone wears a face mask at all times and all fully cover their mouth and nose. covid-19 doesn't stand a chance! 

about the staff:
i've got to admit, i was very nervous about this surgery and still do not have crystal clear vision but the staff here is just amazing. they are so kind comforting, and welcoming. the doctor that preformed my prk surgery was dr. january and he is just amazing. the staff morale is above par, and it's clear that everyone not only loves their job here but they also love each other! i loved seeing them interact with one another in such a friendly yet professional manner. 

communication with the doctor is super important:
first day i met dr. january he gave me his personal cell phone number & he actually answers very promptly! i sent him texts with questions before surgery and i always got very prompt and detailed replies that made me feel more comfortable and always fully answered my question. after surgery my mom called him on a different phone number, on a sunday morning, and he answered right away. that definitely won over my moms heart and comforted her a lot(and she's never met him).  just goes to say this doctor really cares and is here for all of his patients, and i've never seen this down at such a high level before. there is no lack in communication at this office which is 10/10 in my book. 

about prk:
(i'm not a dr this is my general knowlage) 
prk is different from lasik in that there is no "flap" being made on the cornea. instead, the top layer is painlessly brushed off before being treated by the laser and then they put a prescription-less contact lens in your eye. this is less invasive than lasik but does have a greater and more painful recovery time. (pain only lasts about 2-3 days) there are other pros & cons & i recommend researching it, or asking your doctor about the differences. 

my statistics:
my left eye was at -3.5 and right was at -4.0 with astigmatism. i'm 23 years old, am a masters of accounting student and i am taking an online class through out all of this. (and live & home) 

my personal experience: 
(everyone's eyes are different & your experience could differ from mine!)

day 1 i didn't feel much pain and even managed to finish up a little discussion for school before sleeping the rest of the day. (don't recommend using a computer that early on but i didn't have a choice) my most painful days were days 2(night) till day 4 (morning) & i slept a majority of the day though days 1-4. (if i wasn't sleeping i stayed in a dark room and would ice my eyes & listen to music or funny podcasts) the xanax they gave me honestly didn't work and i had to resort to taking other medications that did give me great relief! the "pain" for me was a constant burning feeling and was more bothersome and annoying than "painful". but once it's gone, it's gone. by day 5-6 i would get headaches from straining to see because of my blurry vision but it's normal and extra strength tylenol helps a lot!! 
i recommend taking 5-7 days off of work/ school for less stress and so you can give your eyes the best ability to heal (my personal opinion) but by day 5 i was already comfortably looking at my zoomed in computer screen. i have not experienced any dry eye issues yet, and am very good at keeping up with my drops.

i was referred to dr. armin by my health care clinic in west hollywood. i'm used to going to cedars for my back and spine consultations, but i decided to give dr armin in a try. i've read some of the other reviews posted here and they are completely contrary to the experience that i had with the doctors staff. nancy, at dr. armin's office, was as kind, hospitable and responsive as i could ask for. she responded to phone calls and particularly emails with shockingly fast precision. 

in fact, nancy responded to emails both on the weekend and after hours. this is something i have never encountered with any doctors office or medical service provider. ever. she stayed in constant contact with me about getting me in to see the doctor, this time because of covid-19 via a telemedicine call. 

my first appointment with dr armin was thorough in that he asked a wide range of questions regarding my previous spinal health, going back almost 30 years. based on the information i gave him about my recent injury, he scheduled an mri which, being in a considerable amount of pain, happened within one week. after we received the mri results, nancy was quick to schedule a follow-up appointment for dr armin to review the mri with me. 

i have had spinal surgery, and have had chronic back issues for the best part of my life. i'm an active person and re-injure my back about once a year. this time was different, extraordinarily painful. the doctor reviewed the mri with me in a way that was completely and utterly thorough. we discussed each vertebrae and each disc. he reviewed the health of each vertebrae and each disc with me in detail that was almost exhausting, but it was extraordinary. he gave me a very clear and concise picture of the health of my spine, and gave me advice on how to proceed forward that was very clear. the medicine he prescribed when i first injured my back, and the follow-up appointment to review my mri seem to be completely on point. i am able to function with much less pain and for now, he said that he recommends i avoid any surgery. he recommended a wide variety of preventative procedures and that i stay away from my very favorite activity, doing sit-ups! 

his friendliness, kindness and seemingly genuine concern for the state of my health was quite refreshing. i did not feel like just another patient, or like a faceless person sitting in a waiting room waiting for 5 minutes with a doctor that rushes through his examination. i felt a genuine concern from him for the state of my health and the health of my spine.

i'm not usually moved to write reviews like this, especially one this long. but in the world of overbooked, over taxed, underpaid people, this doctor showed up for me as did his assistant nancy. that is rare and it's deeply appreciated!

i am so thankful that i was able to find dr. huang during this pandemic. he may have literally saved my life by making the correct diagnosis and getting me off the wrong medications that was prescribed by other doctors. 

in early february of 2020, i had an endoscopy done by a gastroenterologist, and about a week after, i started noticing some shortness of breath and also felt a swollen lymph node behind my ear.to make a long story short, fast forward to march of 2020, in the midst of the covid pandemic,i had difficulty breathing and a fever which led me to believe that i may have had been infected with covid19. ultimately, after my lab test result tested negative for covid but indicated klebsiella pneumoniae bacteria, i went to see a pulmonologist at ucla where an x-ray of my lungs were taken to rule out pneumonia. although, the pulmonologist from ucla did not listen to my lungs, he prescribed an antibiotic given the bacteria found in my nose, and asthma medication for breathing problems (even though i had tested negative for asthma couple of years ago by this same doctor) after my breathing condition did not improve, i reached out to a different pulmonologist in glendale who provided telemedicine consults. the second doctor prescribed more asthma medication and ultimately told me to take a repeated x-ray and repeat covid test after my condition did not improve. after the chest xray came out clean for the second time, the doctor in glendale told me he did not know what the problem was and told me to hang in there or go to urgent care. by this time, i had slept only 5 days out of the last 15 days and lost over 10 pounds because of severe breathing problems, sleep deprivation and no appetite. 

then out of desperation at 6:00 am, after having stayed up all night, i searched for another pulmonologist and fortunately found dr. huang on yelp and reached out to him by email. surprisingly, dr. huang got back to me right away and saw me the same day through zoom video conference. dr. huang patiently listened to my history regarding the onset of symptoms  and complaints and told me that if one of the asthma medication he prescribed did not improve my condition within the next few days, then he would see me to figure out what was going on. after symptoms did not improve, i went in for an evaluation and dr. huang actually listened to my lungs using a stethoscope and also conducted a lung function test himself. after a comprehensive evaluation and a lung function test, dr. huang told me that i likely had some form of upper respiratory infection before which may have caused breathing problems and fever, but at the time of his evaluation, my lungs sounded normal and i should not be having such severe breathing problems. he told me that what may be going on is that the asthma medication that i was prescribed was causing anxiety and panic attachs which was making my breathing problems worse - causing a vicious cycle - breathing problem so take more asthma medicine which causes more anxiety which makes breathing problems worse. 

after i was taken off the medication, my breathing problems improved significantly. although, it took weeks to deal with getting over the psychological component of having had breathing problems and panic attacks, i am now almost fully recovered. 

dr. huang was so patient, kind, and methodical in the manner in which he diagnosed my condition in the midst of the covid pandemic. it was so difficult to find a doctor who was willing to actually listen to my lungs during this covid pandemic and give me a correct diagnosis. i cannot thank dr. huang enough. had i gone several more days without sleep, i'm not sure if i would still be alive today.

also, there was zero structure on the weekends (again because of covid), but what about adapting to family zoom meetings, therapy sessions, or 12 step meetings? nope, the therapist wasn't even there on sundays.... we literally sat around doing nothing recovery related. 

speaking of therapy: i was promised 1-2 sessions a week and, over 3 weeks, should have had an average of 4.5 sessions.... i had 2.  there was another client who had been there 5 weeks & also only had 2 sessions.

i wrote a 6 page letter to maddie & katy last tuesday 5/19, and both were let go by friday. i've been told it had nothing to do with my letter, but rather it was something that had been ongoing for sometime. they only opened last september, so that must mean since the beginning?!!! i kind of got the sense my letter was sent up the chain of command by a counselor i shared it with the day before our meeting (5/18), but that's just speculation:

we even had a client who was caught stealing from others & no reprimands were made. it was an ongoing theme of poor/addict behavior with him, and i was amazed it was allowed to continue.

another staff member would talk about his sexcapades, during the virus, and it only made me think of the risk he was putting us all in!!! was he wearing a mask & social distancing? (obviously not). the first day this staff member came in (following the two ladies being let go) his first comment was "ok, no more katy.... i guess that means staff can workout here again!!!" it's crazy that was his first concern.

they forced me to go to parks, and outings, during the pandemic. during which almost all of the clients chose not to wear the masks they had brought.... again, zero control. the reason i couldn't stay behind at the house was because of a 30 minute window with no staff on duty. at $1,000 a day (per person x 6).... they should be able to figure out those 30 minutes & so much more.

i've struggled (unsuccessfully) with aud (alcohol use disorder) for 30-something years. finally, in 2014 i discovered sinclair method (https://www.the-sinclair-method.com/), which turned out to be a lifesaver. my drinking quickly went down to safe levels and i started to have alcohol free days several times a week. for 5.5 years i was a social drinker, a "normie" in aa speak. 

some life events led to me developing a serious depression and covid lockdown became the last straw. in the beginning of april i stopped taking my medication; from there, my drinking quickly escalated and turned into a heavy 6 weeks binge ending in er, icu and a 10 days detox. after i got back home on may 24, i wanted to make sure that sinclaire is still working (i still had some meds and started taking them right away); i had 3 drinks on the first day, then it went 1, 1, 0, 1, 0 - amazing, considering my condition before the detox. 

by then, i found an outpatient program (iop) at good sam behavioral. i was surprised to learn that dr cecil a. bradley, who prescribed me naltrexone all these years, is the medical director of this program. the program seemed very useful since a) it is in person, no zoom, b) i could address my underlying emotional issues and c) i could get an extended medical leave, since i was not ready to get back to work yet. on thursday, may 28 i was admitted; i was very open about what i've been doing before, what brought me there and about my intentions (go back on sinclaire, since it works great and aa stopped working for me at some point). everybody seemed to be open-minded, accepting and approving of my course of treatment. some even wrote down the name of my method and said they were curious and want to learn more about it. 

on friday noon dr bradley showed up, took me to his office and told me that their program is based on full abstinence and if i kept up the controlled drinking, i'd have to leave. he said there are alternatives to aa and suggested some other program - he just could remember it's name. he is in his 80s and seems to forget things. i promised to think about it over the weekend and tell him about my decision on monday. after all, at this point i could possibly refrain from drinking for the duration of the program.

however, on monday my case manager handed me a recovery plan with mandatory conditions: attend at least 3 meetings a week, find a sponsor and report progress at each morning session. i told her i don't do aa, and i was told to go talk to dr bradley, and again he gave me a dilemma: full abstinence and meetings or leave the program. "if you don't want aa, there is this other program - can't remember it's name... rational recovery?" "- smart recovery?" "- yes, this must be it". "- how is it better than aa?". "- i don't know. we require full abstinence and meetings". so i informed him that i'm quitting and went home.

this got me thinking: 1) why did dr bradley prescribe naltrexone all these years and even wrote me another 3 refills on that monday if he disapproves on sinclair method so much? 2) how does a doctor send a patient to some program can't even remember the name of? did he do any research or he really doesn't care? 3) why did they admit me at all, knowing full well my intentions and dr bradley's position and giving me false hope? 4) what kind of doctors put a patient into completely unscientific, faith-based programs with abysmal success rates and force him to abandon something that is proven to work for 80% and this patient in particular?

so i googled dr bradley and discovered that the medical board of california twice has suspended his license, once in 1990 and second time in 2007 (http://www.psychcrime.org/news/index.php?vd=32&t=california+disciplines+psychiatrist+cecil+bradley) he also was known to be sending referrals to life choices and working at red road recovery, two rehabs run by the same person, richard franko, who has no certifications and is a drug addict himself. life choices were reported to california's dhcs for "making parolees assist in human like slave duties as a condition of not sending these clients back to prison. dhcs investigators heard from people they interviewed that franko had indeed used clients for personal benefit and, in doing so, compromised their sobriety." (https://www.sanjoseinside.com/news/rehab-owners-who-lost-license-amid-shocking-allegations-deny-charges-get-back-to-business/)

makes you wonder, how does a doctor like cecil bradley ends up a medical director in well-respected hospital like good sam? i would not recommend going to good sam in- or outpatient behavioral programs until they replace him. the rest of the staff seems to be great, but there is nothing they could do to help me under current leadership.

the pts at go beyond physical therapy are some of the best physical therapists that i have been referred to by an md.

they "go beyond" to help patients achieve results to improve or resolve both acute and chronic issues!

each pt -- dr. korey pieper, joann tippett, and dr. ben stein -- assess and treat patients, then tailor their sessions per individual needs, modifying exercises as needed during each session. 

they also take detailed notes and progress updates. there are no pas here so you're assured of receiving experienced treatment done well!

the sessions are 45 minutes in duration (the initial consultation is 45 minutes to 60 minutes in duration.)

since each pt has a different focus, patients are able to utilize them as a team, either staying with one pt or transitioning to another pt within the practice.

(that's something that i've never seen before!)

--korey pieper, the owner, is a doctor of physical therapy with almost 15 years of experience who is constantly adding to her skillset by learning new techniques and honing her current skills.

korey is kind, professional, and adept at what she does and wants to see her clients recover from injuries and prevent them from future injuries.

she utilizes art -- active release technique, which is a soft tissue-based massage technique that treats muscles, tendons, ligaments, fascia, and nerves.

(art is what sets korey apart. this is what made the difference in my healing process.)

--joann tippett joined the practice over a year ago and has been an amazing addition to go beyond! she has a masters of physical therapy and over 20 years of experience.

joann is talented, effective, and efficient and is methodical in consistently re-evaluating her clients needs with each and every treatment and switching up exercises as needed.

she is extensively trained to treat injuries for the lower back, pelvis, and sacroiliac joint (sij). she is also kinesio tape certified, which means that she'll correctly and skillfully apply the kt to alleviate pain.

(sij treatment is what sets joann apart. her ability to evaluate and work on this has been beyond beneficial!)

she also utilizes pilates for rehab and she is also a certified tai chi instructor.

--ben stein is a doctor of physical therapy and joined the practice several months ago after doing his final clinical rotation at go beyond physical therapy!

doc_text:
renown medical center delivers a ridiculous amount of babies every day (4,063 in the year 2016), especially with being one of the main hospitals in reno (next to st. mary's) and from experience, i can easily see that they know what they're doing.

i'm the mother of three children and two of them were born at renown medical center.  my experiences were nothing short of amazing.  the ease of check in, skill level of the doctors, nurses and staff, resources available, and level of comfort all contributed to my amazing experiences and i would easily come back to renown if i ever planned on having another child.

my second child, arrived in half the time as my first child. instead of 12 hrs., he arrived in 6 hrs. i was at home laboring it out when my water broke and i knew he would come out shortly.  my dear sister zoomed us to the emergency section of the hospital knowing i wouldn't have time to check in and upon arrival, someone with a chair wheeled me into the delivery room.  the nurses heard me coming down the hall and my sister said they all quickly flocked together in a group, waiting to receive me.

they transferred me to the bed and immediately called the doctor.  the doctor arrived promptly and was very skillful with how he delivered my baby.  he did a technique that prevented tares and i couldn't have been happier since my first birthing experience left me in pain with a third degree tare.  asking your doctor ahead of time about ways to prevent tares could be beneficial so as to minimize healing time post delivery.

after my baby came out, the nurses quickly wiped him with towels and placed him on my chest.  bonding occurs right away and it is said that skin to skin contact also helps calm babies while keeping them warm and helps trigger your milk supply for breastfeeding.  they also applied antibiotic eye drops to prevent eye infections.

while holding my baby, the doctor came in and made sure the placenta came out.  one firm press to my stomach did the trick and the placenta slipped right out.

shortly after, the nurses took him to a table right next to my bed. there, they suctioned out extra fluids to help him breath better, took some measurements, and made sure everything was normal.

after being asked some questions, i was transferred to my recovery room.

in recovery, the nurse assisted me with my first bathroom break and gave me some instruction on how to care for myself.  the bathroom was fully stocked with everything i needed-underwear, pads, wash bottles, gowns and towels.   after, she offered me an ice pack for my bottom and i was so thankful since it was so soothing.

with my second baby, my husband went along with the nurses for his first bath. with the third baby, i was able to watch my baby's first bath.

they monitored me and my baby closely to make sure our vitals were on point and to make sure i was feeling ok and that i wasn't bleeding excessively.

a lactation consultant visited me to assist me with breastfeeding and any questions i had.  renown does have alternatives and resources to breastfeeding of you're unable to.

my doctor visited me the following day to see my progress and gave the o.k. to go home.  they monitor you for a minimum of 24 hrs. to make sure everything is fine but mothers usually stay 24-48 hrs. after birth.

it took a total of 10 minutes from the time i arrived to the time my baby came out.  with such little time, renown was able to deliver in all areas.  i was so impressed with how prepared they were.  there's nothing more comforting than knowing you have people you can depend on to get you through your birthing experience.

i gave birth to my three children without epidural and i wouldn't have done it any other way.  of course i was scared of the unknowns of pain that i would experience but i knew it was pain that i could handle and pain that would be worthwhile.

there are many options available for pain management at renown and different methods of giving birth.

with my second delivery at renown, i made sure to allow extra time to check in.  i went in through the front of entrance of the hospital and was checked into a screening room where they determined that i was far along to be admitted.  this time around, they called my doctor (information on hand from pre-registration) who made it just in time to deliver my third baby.  i gave birth yet again and couldn't have been happier with the service given.

renown's doctors, nurses and staff exceeded my expectations.  the beautiful hospital allowed for my husband to sleep overnight with me and the snack room (accessible to only mothers), was a pleasant surprise.

https://www.skillexpertiseandtechnology.com/obreg/

pregnancy guide made by renown:
https://www.renown.org/wp-content/uploads/pregnancyguide.pdf

*don't forget to bring baby's car seat and to install the base prior to giving birth

i've been here 3 or 4 times over the past few years, i tend to get strep throat (or something similar) about once a year and it's not worth a trip to my primary physician (very simple diagnosis and treatment).  i've had no problem with the care received, but i do have a problem with the billing practices -- which seem to have changed significantly in the past year.

i have a high deductible insurance plan and i pay out of pocket at the "negotiated rate" until i hit my deductible.  in the past i've paid about $100 out of pocket for a routine visit to get a quick strep test and get a prescription for antibiotics (whether or not strep test was a strong positive).

this year i got a statement for $564.90, minus 1) insurance adjustment of $182.81 and 2) "insurance pending" of $175.00.  so total due is $207.90.  but the statement isn't itemized at all.  i called the number on the bill to request an itemized statement, but either no answer, voicemail full, or no callback after leaving voicemail.  their payment center is not staffed to handle anything by phone.

so i logged onto my insurance site to see the claim and the non-discounted billed amount is:  1) $321.90 for medical visit, 2) $68 for laboratory services, and 3) $175 for laboratory services.  i was also billed separately by the lab for about $75, but after my insurance discount i paid about $5.  this was for 5 minutes with the nurse (temp, bp, swab) and less than 5 minutes with the doctor.  (in the past i've also been seen by nurse practitioner or mid-level provider, doctor was not necessary for this).

i called my insurance to ask if these charges are reasonable and they seemed to imply it was normal.  they also confirmed they're not paying anything since i didn't meet my deductible (which is expected).  so i hope i don't get billed separately for $175 "insurance pending".

also, on each visit they send the throat swab to the lab and promise to call me with results, but they never call.  seems like a pointless step unless you don't get better on the antibiotics.

and...  i paid the invoice, but since they don't answer the phone you can only pay by mail.  there is no option to pay online.  hard to believe given the amount of revenue they're bringing in.

so if i happen to go here again (not likely) i will claim to be uninsured and pay cash...  which would have been $175.00 per their website.  if you present your insurance card they see $$$$.  

more likely i'll end up at minuteclinic or telemedicine.

it is with regret that the first yelp review i write is a negative one, and i am inclined to write it nonetheless. i first contacted holt counseling center in january of 2020 as a potential site for my mft practicum. i was met with nothing but rudeness and dismissiveness from the main coordinator, bonnie. i found her to be pushy, short tempered and irritable to put it nicely. in response to any of my questions, i was met with a tone of voice that made me feel like the dumbest person alive for even asking. regardless of how awful the phone call went, she surprised me with inviting me to a supervision group to get started with practicum...huh? no request for an interview, no request for a resume. just show up and we would be good to go. the result of this phone call gave many red flags and i decided not to pursue an internship with them. ultimately, i found two placements and have been happily working through practicum with them instead.  

fast forward to the covid-19 pandemic, and i received a phone call from bonnie regarding practicum yet again at the beginning of may 2020. she informed me many therapists were leaving and they were in search of new interns. she was pleasant during this conversation, and i began to think i had read our initial call incorrectly. i was asked to submit my resume, dl, ssc, and practicum agreement via email and was told about the in person meeting on may 31st (mind you, shelter-in-place has not been fully lifted.) the in person meeting struck me as odd, as i currently have two other placements who are fully telehealth and are not planning on resuming in person sessions, trainings or meetings any time soon. when i asked what safety measures would be in place, her response was "well people can wear a mask if they want to. our lodi office is definitely cleaner than our stockton one, haha." red flag #1,000,000,000.

two weeks after our early may phone call, i received a reminder call and spoke with bonnie on the phone regarding the meeting in which i told her i was still considering how i felt about meeting in person. we ended the call without incident, with bonnie reminding me of the date and time. 

today, may 31st, 2020, i received a missed phone call and a text from bonnie in the afternoon that was incredibly direct, rude and was riddled with false information. she texted me that she had tried to get a hold of me numerous times without hearing back from me...(um...no you didn't), and that she needed all of my info. and if i was still going to work for them (um...i already sent it to you weeks before). i called back and left a message, politely reminding her that all of my paperwork was already done and submitted per our conversation a couple of weeks earlier (and, in fact, i had not heard back from her). she called me back within 10 minutes. i asked if she received my message, and i was met with "hah, no i saw it but didn't listen to it so.." k.... i reiterated my message and she had the audacity to challenge me by saying, "actually, hon, i've called multiple times and you have not responded at all to any of my calls." in which i responded, "i'm wondering if there might be a mistake and if there is another cristina, because i did talk to you on the phone last week and submitted all of my information to you for practicum, as well as my interest and understanding of the in person meeting. i clearly remember the phone call." her response: "yeah actually no, i have not been able to reach you at all, but whatever, are you coming to the meeting or not?" as frustrated with this woman as i was, i managed to hold it together and respond with, "i will not be coming. i do not feel it is safe right now due to covid. i have a family and we made this decision in our best interest, however, i would be open and willing to attend the meeting via zoom as an option." she responded by talking over me and cutting me off with, "uh, yeah, no zoom is terrible and clients don't like that. we need to open, that's just what we are going to do." my response, "i have two other placements who are fully on zoom and it has worked beautifully for all supervision, trainings, and client sessions. i will not be coming today." resulting response from her, "this isn't the placement for you. click." 

really? do not challenge my integrity or honesty. do not gaslight me. do not imply that i am not an honest person. for anyone considering interning here, don't. i dodged a big bullet with this one. thank you, holt counseling, for reminding me i am unavailable for rudeness and disrespect. i'll be awesome someplace else.
